text: The sun slipped low. The bush turned gold and soft.
Sunny wandered where the fallen logs lay still.
Beside a log she saw a stripy back,
a little someone snuffling in the bark.
A numbat, small and quick, with bands of white,
and a long thin nose for finding tiny snacks.
His bushy tail stood up like a little flag,
as he pattered softly round the sleeping log.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “You're up nice and late.”
“Just one last look,” he said, “before my bed.”
He showed her round his log, all snug inside,
lined with leaves and soft with strips of bark.
“When stars come out,” he said, “I curl up here,
where it's warm and dark and safe the whole night through.”
So Sunny watched the sky turn dusky blue,
and felt the bush grow quiet all around.
The little numbat yawned a tiny yawn,
his stripy back all soft in the fading light.
He crept inside his hollow log to sleep,
his bushy tail tucked warm around his nose.
Sunny found a nest of leaves nearby,
and snuggled down beside the sleeping log.
The bush was still. The first stars blinked awake.
Everything was peaceful, warm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy in the gentle dark.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beside the little numbat,
both of them dreaming in the quiet night.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little numbat.
Goodnight, sleepy bush. Goodnight, little one.
